task.title: Generate a 30s product promo film
task.goal: Cinematic, warm-toned, foregrounding the product's material quality (metal/glass)

userStory.trigger: Marketing wants a 30s product film for next week's pitch
userStory.goal: Get a usable rough-cut direction before committing to a full render
userStory.reads: The agent's read on your creative intent: the tone decision, the two style directions in play, and where it's uncertain or prone to glitches
userStory.acts: Pick style A/B / adjust the tone decision / flag shots to re-render

observablePrimitives.label: Creative brief: cinematic, warm-toned, foreground material quality

nodes.title: Intent as understood: cinematic + warm-toned + 16:9, foregrounding metal/glass material quality

evidence.label: brief keywords align with the moodboard's leaning

nodes.title: Tone reconsidered
nodes.to: Golden-hour warm light + shallow depth of field, a texture-forward piece
nodes.rationale: The brand guidelines call for restraint, premium feel, low saturation; the bright commercial look clashes with that, while warm light and shallow DoF bring out the metal/glass material quality.

nodes.title: Tone: golden-hour warm light + shallow depth of field + slow push-in

evidence.label: matches the brand's restraint / low saturation

nodes.title: Two style directions for you to pick: A photoreal texture / B miniature fantasy
nodes.falsification: B (miniature fantasy) is more striking but departs from photorealism; if the brand can accept a non-photoreal treatment, go B, otherwise A. Your call.

nodes.title: Hand close-ups and product logo text are prone to artifacts
nodes.falsification: If we switch to product-only shots that avoid hands and composite the logo in post rather than generating it, the risk goes away; the current shot list has 2 hand close-ups.

nodes.title: How the closing logo is presented is undecided
nodes.needs: Is the logo a live-action texture composite, a particle convergence, or a clean freeze-frame? Need your direction.

nodes.title: Bright, high-saturation commercial-ad look
nodes.reason: Clashes with the brand's "restrained, premium, low-saturation" tone, and it flattens the metal/glass material quality.

outcome.label: Current direction · Grounded
outcome.text: Tone set as a golden-hour warm-light, shallow-DoF texture piece; style directions A/B await your pick.
outcome.recommendation: Run the full render once A/B is chosen; switch hand shots to product-only and composite the logo in post to avoid artifacts.

steps.label: Understand the intent
steps.hint: First anchor the brief and moodboard as a requirement.

steps.label: Tone inflection
steps.hint: Aha: the brand guidelines ⇒ a warm-light shallow-DoF texture piece, and the bright commercial look settles.

steps.label: Tone crystallizes
steps.hint: The tone crystallizes into a grounded decision, with the 4-frame test re-renderable for verification.

steps.label: Needs your call
steps.hint: Honestly leaves it: style A/B, the artifact risk, and the ending all await your decision.
